name: regenerate
title: Regenerate minutes
description: Bring a meeting's minutes up to date as a background job (kind `regenerate`). The deterministic stages (ffmpeg preprocessing, transcription, diarization) run idempotently first: each is skipped when its recorded input hashes and parameters are unchanged and only runs when it never ran (a meeting stopped with auto_process=false, a process job that failed) or when set_meeting_config changed its parameters (transcription_engine, diarization_engine, language, vocab_hints). Then alignment → LLM integration → minutes generation run with the same idempotency: a new minutes version is appended only when something changed — existing versions are never overwritten. Use it after set_meeting_config or register_context, to process a meeting stopped with auto_process=false, or to retry a failed process job. `force=true` re-runs alignment, integration and generation even when their inputs are unchanged (still appending a new version); preprocessing and transcription are never forced. `reason` is recorded in manifest.regenerations. `scope` is the scope selector (default deny: a scoped meeting needs its scope in the request). `request_id` is the client-generated idempotency key: repeating the call returns the same job_id. On failure returns an error_envelope (isError=true) with code: not_found (unknown meeting), scope_denied (the request does not cover the meeting's scope), busy (the meeting is still recording, or a job is already queued / running for it), policy_violation (the configured llm_provider or engines are not allowed by external_send_policy — nothing is silently downgraded), engine_unavailable (configured engine / provider not installed), invalid_argument, internal. Failures inside the job are reported by get_job_status.

force.description: Re-run all stages from alignment even if inputs/params are unchanged (default false).

reason.description: Free-text reason recorded in manifest.regenerations (e.g. "added Notion transcript").

job_id.description: The enqueued regenerate job; poll with get_job_status.
